extra.message: Ad-hoc search condition (outStandingAmountPercentageCondition) supplied in the POST JSON body is concatenated directly into the SQL string. The validator AdHocQueryDataValidator.java:121 incorrectly calls isNotOneOfTheseValues(AD_HOC_SEARCH_QUERY_CONDITIONS), which rejects valid operators and lets arbitrary strings (e.g. "= 1 UNION SELECT ...") pass. SQL injection.

Ad-hoc search condition (outstandingAmountCondition) from the POST JSON body is concatenated directly into the SQL string without sanitisation. AdHocQueryDataValidator.java:154 uses the inverted isNotOneOfTheseValues call, so malicious operators pass validation. SQL injection.

The sqlSearch request query parameter (ClientsApiResource.retrieveAll) is placed into the WHERE clause with raw string concatenation (extraCriteria = " and (" + sqlSearch + ")") and then executed by jdbcTemplate. Only cosmetic replaceAll of display_name is performed. SQL injection.

The orderBy/sortOrder query parameters are appended to the SQL ORDER BY clause with no allow-list validation (sqlBuilder.append(" order by ").append(searchParameters.getOrderBy())). Arbitrary SQL can be injected. SQL injection.
The sqlSearch request parameter (LoansApiResource.retrieveAll) is concatenated into the WHERE clause and executed by jdbcTemplate with no escaping. SQL injection.
The orderBy/sortOrder query parameters are appended raw to the SQL ORDER BY clause with no allow-list validation. SQL injection.
The sqlSearch request parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL WHERE clause (sqlBuilder.append(" and (").append(sqlQueryCriteria)) and executed by jdbcTemplate. SQL injection.
The orderBy/sortOrder query parameters are appended raw to the SQL ORDER BY clause with no validation. SQL injection.
The sqlSearch request parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL WHERE clause (extraCriteria.append(" and ( ").append(sqlSearch)) and executed by jdbcTemplate. SQL injection.
The sqlSearch request parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL WHERE clause of the staff query and executed by jdbcTemplate. SQL injection.

The report name (from @PathParam("reportName") on /runreports/{reportName}) is concatenated directly into the SQL used to look up the report definition ("... where " + type + "_name = '" + name + "'") and executed via jdbcTemplate.queryForRowSet. SQL injection.
The report name is concatenated directly into the SQL "... where report_name = '" + reportName + "'" and executed via jdbcTemplate.queryForRowSet. SQL injection.

checkUserPermissionForReport() skips the report permission check entirely when the parameterType query parameter is true, allowing any authenticated user to reach getSql(reportName,"parameter") and supply the SQL-injectable reportName. Missing authorization / access-control bypass.

Report parameters taken from the request (R_* query parameters, RunreportsApiResource.getReportParams) are substituted into the stored report SQL via GenericDataServiceImpl.replace, which performs a raw string replacement with no escaping or quoting (GenericDataServiceImpl.java:91-106). Attacker-controlled parameter values are injected into the executed SQL. SQL injection.
The surveyName path parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL query ("... and registered_table_name='" + surveyName + "'") and executed via jdbcTemplate.queryForRowSet. SQL injection.
The order query parameter (DatatablesApiResource) is concatenated directly into the SQL statement (sql = sql + " order by " + order) and executed. No validation is applied. SQL injection.

The uploaded file name (multipart filename, DocumentManagementApiResource.createDocument/updateDocument) is concatenated onto the storage directory with no sanitisation of path separators or "..". A filename such as "../../../../etc/x" escapes the intended directory; writeFileToFileSystem() then writes to that path (line 164 new FileOutputStream(new File(fileLocation))). Path traversal leading to arbitrary file write.

The image file name (multipart filename, ImagesApiResource.createImage/updateImage) is concatenated onto the storage directory without sanitising ".." or path separators, then written via FileOutputStream(new File(fileLocation)) at line 164. Path traversal / arbitrary file write.

mergeTemplate (POST /templates/{templateId}) performs no permission check (no validateHasReadPermission and no command wrapper), unlike every other method in this class. Any authenticated user can trigger server-side template compilation/merge. Missing authorization.

URLs produced from template mappers (getCompiledMapFromMappers, lines 90-108) are passed to new URL(url).openConnection() and fetched without any allow-list or validation. Because mergeTemplate has no authorization check, a crafted template/mapper causes server-side requests to arbitrary internal hosts. SSRF.

The current authenticated user's plaintext password is read from Authentication.getCredentials() (enabled by erase-credentials="false" in securityContext.xml) and installed as a JVM-global Authenticator that will respond to any server the SSRF/URL fetch contacts, leaking the credential. Sensitive data exposure.

AlwaysTrustManager accepts any TLS certificate (empty checkServerTrusted) and TrustingHostnameVerifier.verify() unconditionally returns true. Certificates/hostnames are never validated, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks on template-driven HTTPS requests. Improper certificate validation.

configureClient() installs a trust-all X509TrustManager (empty checkServerTrusted/checkClientTrusted) and a HostnameVerifier that always returns true for all outbound webhook/Twilio calls. TLS endpoint identity is never verified (CWE-295). Additionally createWebHookService(url) at line 113-118 uses an admin-configured URL with setEndpoint(url), enabling SSRF.

The taxonomy mapping expression stored via PUT /mixmapping (MixTaxonomyMappingApiResource.updateTaxonomyMapping) is evaluated with a Nashorn JavaScript ScriptEngine (script engine obtained at line 48, allowing Java interop). A mapping value such as java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec(...) yields remote code execution. Code injection.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: retrieveCode() fetches a code by id without any permission check, while the sibling retrieveCodes() calls validateHasReadPermission. Any authenticated user can read code data. Missing authorization.

retrieveOne() returns an SMS message by id with no permission check, unlike retrieveAll() which calls validateHasReadPermission. Any authenticated user can read SMS message content. Missing authorization.

retrieveAccount() and retrieveAllAccounts() return account data for any account id/type without any permission check (the injected platformSecurityContext is only used by the write methods). Broken access control: any authenticated user can read any account. Missing authorization.

getJournalData() returns teller/cashier journal data for arbitrary officeId/tellerId/cashierId with no permission check; the injected PlatformSecurityContext (field securityContext) is never used. Missing authorization / IDOR.

The CORS filter sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * for all responses and reflects any client-supplied Access-Control-Request-Headers value back in Access-Control-Allow-Headers, enabling permissive cross-origin access to the authenticated API. Security misconfiguration.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The request parameter oauth_token is appended unencoded to the failure redirect URL (defaultFailureUrl + "?oauth_token=" + oauthToken) and passed to sendRedirect. An attacker-controlled value containing CR/LF can inject response headers / manipulate the redirect. HTTP response header injection.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: The HTTPS connector uses a hardcoded keystore/truststore password "openmf" (getKeystorePass()) together with the keystore bundled in source resources (/keystore.jks). Hardcoded credential.

retrieveLoanCharge() calls itself recursively (return this.retrieveLoanCharge(loanId, loanChargeId, uriInfo)) instead of delegating to loanChargesApiResource.retrieveLoanCharge as its sibling methods do, causing an unconditional StackOverflowError / denial of service on every request to GET /self/loans/{loanId}/charges/{chargeId}.
